title: More models, fewer authentication detours
summary:
This week made model access easier to navigate, image usage easier to account for, and the growing app ecosystem easier to explore.

Claude Haiku 4.5 joined the model list as `claudyclaude`, supporting text and image input plus tools. Valid Enter tokens gained access to text models and Kontext without model-tier checks, and Enter added `Authorization: Bearer <key>` support. Kontext retains its queue and concurrency limits.

Nectar users gained a `quality=high` option for gptimage, along with higher queue concurrency and a shorter forced interval; other tiers retain medium quality. Image queues gained model-specific concurrency caps, while GPT Image usage and several model pricing records were corrected.

Image and text responses gained a shared set of model and token-usage headers when that data is available. Streaming text can provide usage in HTTP trailers. Together with GPT Image’s actual output-token accounting, this gives developers a clearer picture of their requests.

The API docs now move from a quick start into expanded Python, JavaScript, and cURL examples for text, image, and audio. They also support testing with a Bearer token. The authentication guide and Pollen FAQ clarify key access, and the web-search example now names a search-capable model.
